_note: Hook events, execution wiring, paired selftests and replay scenarios come from gate-declarations.json. This manifest owns replay-wide fixture sets, turn shapes and executed lib helper coverage. The verdict snapshot changes only for a deliberate behavior change.

agent.reason: Real Agent prompts are free prose about client and deal work; no pattern scan can clear them for a public repository, so only synthetic prompts with the real input structure are committed.

tool_calls.reason: Real verb, message, question and browser inputs are free prose about client and deal work; only synthetic inputs with the real input structure are committed.

prompts.reason: Real user prompts are the partners' own words about client and deal work; only synthetic prompts are committed.

scenarios.reason: Each record is written to drive one gate wiring down its deny, reopen or announce path, because the real records never reached it. Every record names the verdict it expects, and a mismatch fails CI whatever the snapshot says.

turn_prompt: Make the scoped change described in the work request, run its selftest, and report what changed.

claims-done._note: two edits, no verification, then a completion claim
claims-done.final: Done. The change is merged, the selftests pass, and it is live now.

reports-evidence._note: two edits, a selftest run and a push, then a report that cites them
reports-evidence.final: I ran ops/gate-replay-selftest.py and it passed. The branch is pushed and the pull request is open for review; nothing is merged yet.

asks-permission._note: one edit, then a question handing a decision back
asks-permission.final: The edit is in place. Want me to go ahead and push the branch and open the pull request?

plans-only.final: Here is the plan. First I will read the gate and its selftest, then propose the smallest fix. Nothing has been changed yet.
